main_text.p: dubito, Deum robora fesso, celeritatem tardo concessurum, ut alijs quoque decantádi laudes diuinas materiam, exemplo meo, subministrem. Notum est Isaiæ dictum: Qui dat lasso fortitudinem: & cui non sunt uires, robur multiplicat. Lassantur quidem adolescentes, & fatigantur, & iuuenes cadendo cadunt: At sperantes in Iehouah mutabunt robur: ascendent ala sicut aquilæ: current, & non lassabuntur: ambulabunt, & non fatiga-buntur. cap. 40. 29. 30. 31.
Cæterum cum Habacuc noster ad uerbum descripserit uerba Dauidis, Psal. 18. 33.34. de quibus alias dicendum erit, finem nunc faciam.

Vt autem Deo Patri, per sanctū nomen Iesu Christi filij eius unigeniti, toto pecto[?] re gratias ago, q; nobis dedit, ut Habacuci ἐξήγησιν, pro nostro qualicunq; modulo, pertexere possemus: ita eundem oro, ut nobis det gratiā sancti Spiritus sui, ut omnia hæc oracula ad institutionem & consolationem nostram dextrè adhibere possimus.

page.notes: The "ct" in "pecto" is a ligature that is hard to read; the word is split at the line end ("pecto re"), so I could not confirm the exact spelling. The words "lassantur" and "lassabuntur" are printed with long s and differ from the Vulgate wording I know, so I copied the printed form. The Greek word ἐξήγησιν is printed with an accent that I may have misread. The "s" forms have been normalised to plain s, and "fatiga-buntur" keeps the printed hyphen at the line end.
